text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** Sources agree that NMC only wins on weight, and often by less than you'd expect.

**Cycle life is the biggest difference**
- LiFePO4 stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles. NMC units are rated for roughly 500-800, and one source says up to 2,000 ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- With daily cycling, 500 cycles lasts under 2 years and 3,000 lasts about 8.
- Check the end point of the rating. "To 70%" promises less than "to 80%" ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Safety**
- In lab tests, LFP cells failed more mildly, with lower peak temperatures and less gas ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- LFP isn't fireproof, and one study found it reached runaway earlier in an overcharge test ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). The failures are less violent, which matters if you keep it indoors or in a vehicle.

**Weight**
- NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram, but the inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way. In one database the median NMC station was only about 10% better per pound ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Another source puts the gap closer to 16% ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- Some LFP stations are lighter per watt-hour than NMC ones, so compare actual specs.

**Cost**
- One retailer database shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). LFP is also far cheaper per rated cycle.

**Cold weather**
- Don't expect chemistry to help much here. Many stations of both types won't charge below 32°F, and the limits depend on the maker. Check the manual.

**When NMC makes sense**
- You want the lightest possible unit for occasional use.
- You find a deeply discounted unit for a few trips a year.
- You already own one that works. There's no need to replace it.

**An example LiFePO4 pick:** the [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station rated for 6,000+ cycles to 80%, with a 2,600 W inverter and a 5-year warranty. It weighs 24.2 kg (about 53 lb) and isn't expandable. It's listed at $899.
